name: Autosomal Recessive Amelia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Recessive Amelia

criteria.description: Complete absence of one or more limbs present at birth
Evidence of autosomal recessive inheritance pattern (family history or genetic testing)
Lack of other syndromic malformations or chromosomal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete limb absence at birth with confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance pattern
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis by identifying causative mutations; exclusion of other syndromes with limb defects is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete absence of one or more limbs (amelia)

searchTerms: absence of limbs on both sides

common.symptomName: Hypoplasia or absence of distal limb segments
searchTerms: underdeveloped or missing hand or foot parts
short or absent fingers or toes

common.symptomName: Shortened long bones in affected limbs

occasional.symptomName: Mild scoliosis secondary to limb asymmetry
searchTerms: mild spine curvature from uneven limbs
slight scoliosis due to limb length difference

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint contractures in residual limb segments
searchTerms: mild joint stiffness in remaining limb parts
limited joint movement in residual limbs

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones due to limb absence
searchTerms: slow motor development due to missing limbs
late motor skills from limb absence

occasional.symptomName: Skin hypoplasia over absent limb areas
searchTerms: thin or underdeveloped skin over missing limbs
skin underdevelopment on absent limb areas

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying causative mutations in limb development genes
imaging: X-rays showing complete absence of limb bones
Ultrasound or MRI confirming absence of limb structures
genetic: Mutations in genes involved in limb bud formation (e.g., WNT3 gene mutations)
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect limb absence
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive transmission

distinguishingFeatures: Absent radius but presence of thumbs
No family history or inheritance pattern

redFlags: Complete absence of multiple limbs detected prenatally
Family history of similar limb defects
Presence of additional congenital anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
references: Superti-Furga A, et al. Limb malformations: molecular genetics and clinical features. Clin Genet. 2019.
